answer: Quadratic staking erosion and substantial liquidity-sink commitments impose super-linear marginal attack costs, ensuring that any Sybil cluster must expend capital disproportionately to potential extracted value. This mechanism constructs a robust economic jetty, where the cost to acquire control, scaling as O(N^2) against a linear N stake, makes any gains ultimately hollow. The protocol's economic security threshold is sustained where this expenditure vastly exceeds speculative profit, serving as a guiding lantern against network subversion.
